# Tests/GameLogicTests/EquipmentAnswers.txt
#
# The shipyard's known answers (D53, D74): what the equipment list offers and what it costs at every economy, government
# and tech level from 0 to 15, and what filling the tank costs, 1,040 answers, as the shipyard's rules (GameLogic/Equipment.h)
# compute them. They were recorded from the rules once a scratch run had shown that the 1987 equipment screen,
# ShowEquipShipScreen, lists the same rows at the same prices for all 1,024 of those systems, and that PayForEquipmentItem
# charges the same for fuel at every level and every price's low byte, with every replay's digests unchanged (ADR-043).
# EquipmentAnswerTests checks them.
#
# The shipyards: 1,024 lines, one for each economy (0-7), government (0-7) and tech level (0-15), in that order:
#
#   shipyard ECONOMY GOVERNMENT TECH ROWS PRICE/RESALE ... (one for each row on sale, from fuel's)
#
#   ROWS    the rows on sale, Elite::EquipmentRowsOnSale of the tech level
#   PRICE   the row's price, in tenths of a credit, Elite::EquipmentPriceTenths of Elite::EquipmentItemAt
#   RESALE  what it sells back for, Elite::ResaleTenths of the price
#
# The fuel: 16 lines, one for each price of a light year, 0 to 255 in steps of 17, the low byte being all the rule reads:
#
#   fuel PRICE FUEL:COST ... (for a tank holding 0, 1, 16, 64, 128, 200, 252, 253, 254 and 255)
#
#   COST  what filling the tank costs, in tenths of a credit, Elite::FuelPriceTenths
#
# Checking: a line that differs fails, naming it and both texts, and so does a count other than 1,040. Recording: with
# OUTPOST_ELITE_RECORD_GUARD set, in one process and never in CI, the test writes the answers instead, keeping this header.
#
